daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

The Corruption Eradication Commission (KPK) arrested Klaten Regent Hamenang in a dawn operation and seized a blue barrel allegedly used to store corruption proceeds. The KPK confiscated Rp 1 billion and also detained a Central Java BPK official in connection with alleged bribes related to government projects and audit oversight. The KPK has already designated suspects from the operation.

  • The Constitutional Court ordered amendments to the Military Justice Law to distinguish clearly between military and common crimes, ruling in favor of a mother whose son died in military custody.
  • The Prabowo administration instructed the Law and Human Rights Minister to review regulations that do not support the president's priority programs and bring them into alignment.
  • A witness testified in court that travel agents received fees of thousands of US dollars per pilgrim and that quotas for hajj officials were sold.
  • A corruption case involving BNPB emergency funds was criticized as a human rights violation.
  • The DPR Commission I characterized the swap of the Army Chief and Vice TNI Commander positions as part of a leadership refresh.
  • The government announced plans to tackle graduate unemployment through a national internship program.

Foreign Policy & Defence

President Prabowo appointed Maruli Simanjuntak as Vice TNI Commander and Tandyo Budi Revita as Army Chief in a leadership swap, with the new KSAD pledging to accelerate the president's priority programs. Indonesia now has ten active four-star generals—seven from the TNI and three from the police. The personnel changes come as analysts assess the trajectory for TNI Commander succession.

  • President Prabowo approved accepting assistance from neighboring countries to combat wildfires, according to the foreign minister.
  • Foreign Minister Nasir confirmed that Indonesia complies with ASEAN wildfire reporting protocols and reports fire management efforts routinely to the regional bloc.
  • Indonesia and Timor-Leste signed an investment treaty to expand economic ties between the two countries.
  • The government urged umrah pilgrims to remain vigilant amid Middle East tensions and prepared contingency plans for Indonesian citizens in Saudi Arabia.
  • Marines captured the deputy regional commander of OPM in a pre-dawn operation in Papua, with the suspect surrendering to authorities.

Other

MSCI opened the possibility of downgrading Indonesia's capital market status and proposed reclassifying it as a standalone market, which could place Indonesia in the same category as Zimbabwe. The Indonesia Stock Exchange responded to the proposed reclassification.

  • Investment Minister Bahlil reported that nickel downstreaming boosted Indonesia's export target to US$45 billion.
  • Indonesia will begin crypto tax data exchange under the OECD's Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework in 2027.
  • Jakarta ranked among the top three most polluted cities in the world this morning as wildfire smoke continues to affect air quality.
  • At least 62,000 toddlers contracted respiratory infections in areas affected by forest and land fires.
  • The Jakarta MRT Phase 2A project remains on schedule despite the discovery of 4,000 archaeological artifacts during construction.
